arxiv-2010-12086.creator: Pavlo Baloh, Lukas Bauer, Lukas Beddrich, Anežka Bendová, Petr Čermák, Korbinian Fellner, Madhu Ghanathe, Octavio Emmanuel Hernández Alvarez, Štefan Hricov, Johanna K. Jochum, Liliia Kotvytska, Sonu Kumar, Ankit Labh, Petr Machovec, Brian R. Pauw, Klaudie Ramszová, Erik Walz, Peter Wild, Czech-Bavar
arxiv-2010-12086.description: Abstract Efforts are rising in opening up science by making data more transparent and more easily available, including the data reduction and evaluation procedures and code. A strong foundation for this is the F.A.I.R. principle, building on Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reuse of digital assets, complemented by the letter T for trustworthyness of the data.

arxiv-2402-13321.title: Rigor with Machine Learning from Field Theory to the Poincaré Conjecture Sergei Gukov a,b, 1 1 1 gukov@theory.caltech.edu , James Halverson c,e, 2 2 2 j.halverson@northeastern.edu , Fabian Ruehle c,d,e, 3 3 3 f.ruehle@northeastern.edu a {}^{a}\; Richard N. Merkin Center for Pure and Applied Mathemat
arxiv-2402-13321.description: Abstract Machine learning techniques are increasingly powerful, leading to many breakthroughs in the natural sciences, but they are often stochastic, error-prone, and blackbox. How, then, should they be utilized in fields such as theoretical physics and pure mathematics that place a premium on rigor and understanding?

arxiv-2409-01978.title: Application of Langevin Dynamics to Advance the Quantum Natural Gradient Optimization Algorithm
arxiv-2409-01978.creator: Oleksandr Borysenko, Mykhailo Bratchenko, Ilya Lukin, Mykola Luhanko, Ihor Omelchenko, Andrii Sotnikov, Alessandro Lomi
arxiv-2409-01978.description: Abstract A Quantum Natural Gradient (QNG) algorithm for optimization of variational quantum circuits has been proposed recently. In this study, we employ the Langevin equation with a QNG stochastic force to demonstrate that its discrete-time solution gives a generalized form of the above-specified algorithm, which we call Momentum-QNG.

arxiv-2411-02929.title: The spectral concentration for damped waves on compact Anosov manifolds
arxiv-2411-02929.creator: Yulin Gong
arxiv-2411-02929.description: Abstract . We study the spectral distribution of damped waves on compact Anosov manifolds. Sjöstrand [ Sjö00 ] proved that the imaginary parts of the majority of the eigenvalues concentrate near the average of the damping function, see also Anantharaman [ Ana10 ] .

arxiv-2503-00996.title: Pure Shape Dynamics: Relational General Relativity
arxiv-2503-00996.creator: Pooya Farokhi, Tim Koslowski, Pedro Naranjo
arxiv-2503-00996.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pooya Farokhi, Tim Koslowski, Pedro Naranjo. We present a Pure Shape Dynamics (PSD) formulation of General Relativity (GR), which implements full relationalism by eliminating absolute scale and external time references from the fundamental description of gravity. Starting from the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formulation, we derive a decoupled dynamical system that governs the evolution of the spatial conformal geometry and relational matter degrees of freedom, while eliminating the total volume and York time as independent dynamical variables.

arxiv-2503-21452.title: Numerical solution of locally loaded Volterra integral equations
arxiv-2503-21452.creator: Byankin Vladislav, Tynda Aleksandr, Sidorov Denis, Dreglea Aliona
arxiv-2503-21452.description: Abstract Volterra’s integral equations with local and nonlocal loads represent the novel class of integral equations that have attracted considerable attention in recent years. These equations are a generalisation of the classic Volterra integral equations, which were first introduced by Vito Volterra in the late 19th century.

arxiv-2506-00070.title: Robot-R1: Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced Embodied Reasoning in Robotics
arxiv-2506-00070.creator: Dongyoung Kim, Sumin Park, Huiwon Jang, Jinwoo Shin, Jaehyung Kim, Younggyo Seo
arxiv-2506-00070.description: Abstract Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have recently shown great promise in advancing robotics by combining embodied reasoning with robot control. A common approach involves training on embodied reasoning tasks related to robot control using Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT). However, SFT datasets are often heuristically constructed and not explicitly optimized for improving robot control.

arxiv-2508-15485.title: Polymer translocation through extended patterned pores: scaling of the total translocation time
arxiv-2508-15485.creator: Andri Sharma 1,2, Abhishek Chaudhuri 1, Rajeev Kapri 1
arxiv-2508-15485.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andri Sharma 1,2, Abhishek Chaudhuri 1, Rajeev Kapri 1. We study the translocation of a flexible polymer through extended patterned pores using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We consider cylindrical and conical pore geometries that can be controlled by the angle of the pore apex α \alpha .

pmc-10565545.title: Management of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma: challenges and strategies for optimal outcomes
pmc-10565545.creator: Jae Hyun Yoon, Sung Kyu Choi
pmc-10565545.description: Although hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is associated with a poor prognosis, management of early-stage HCC is often successful with highly efficacious treatment modalities such as liver transplantation, surgical resection, and radiofrequency ablation. However, unfavorable clinical outcomes have been observed under certain circumstances, even after efficient treatment.

pmc-11340222.title: Is capsulectomy necessary for symptom improvement in patients undergoing implant removal for systemic symptoms?
pmc-11340222.creator: Patricia McGuire, Caroline Glicksman
pmc-11340222.description: A case of symptom improvement after implant removal without capsulectomy is presented with a review of the literature. Case report: A 58-year-old woman presented requesting implant removal for systemic symptoms that she attributed to her smooth, saline, breast implants. The implants had been placed in a submuscular position in 2009 for aesthetic reasons (Figure 1).

pmc-11611744.title: Coexistence of Pemphigus Foliaceus and Bullous Pemphigoid: A Case Report
pmc-11611744.creator: Jinxiang Yuan, Xinyi Yao, Lvye Liu, Junling Zhang
pmc-11611744.description: Pemphigus foliaceus (PF) and bullous pemphigoid (BP) are distinct autoimmune bullous skin diseases mediated by autoantibodies targeting adhesion molecules in desmosomes and hemidesmosomes structural proteins in the epidermal-basement membrane zone, respectively. The coexistence of PF and BP is rare. We present the case of a 72-year-old male with clinical and histological features of both PF and BP.

pmc-11715897.title: Health related quality of life in an at‐risk population during an intervention study and extended follow‐up ‐ the Finnish Geriatric Intervention Study to Prevent Cognitive Impairment and Disability (FINGER)
pmc-11715897.creator: Jenni Lehtisalo, Tiia Ngandu, Francesca Mangialasche, Tiina Laatikainen, Timo Strandberg, Riitta Antikainen, Jaakko Tuomilehto, Hilkka Soininen, Dharma Singh Khalsa, Miia Kivipelto
pmc-11715897.description: BackgroundThe multidomain lifestyle intervention in the Finnish Geriatric Intervention Study to Prevent Cognitive Impairment and Disability (FINGER) showed positive effects on health‐related quality of life (HRQL) during the 2‐year intervention, particularly physical functioning. Our aim was to study how these benefits were maintained over an extended follow‐up.

pmc-12530417.title: How to measure the core functions of primary care in low-income and middle-income country settings
pmc-12530417.creator: Robert Mash, Innocent Besigye, Kéfilath Bello, Anna Galle
pmc-12530417.description: The core functions of primary care are first contact access, comprehensiveness, continuity, coordination and person-centredness. These five core functions are highlighted as essential aspects of quality by the new WHO’s measurement framework. In low-income and middle-income countries, the core functions are rarely measured and routinely collected data does not support their measurement.

pmc-12976367.title: Strategies to control cellular spatial organization in microphysiological systems
pmc-12976367.creator: Hung Dong Truong, Zhixing Ge, Elgene Chng, Y-Van Tran, Yusheng Zhang, Chwee Teck Lim
pmc-12976367.description: Spatial organization is fundamental to tissue physiology, as it governs how cells migrate, grow, differentiate, and interact within their native environments. In living tissues, cells are positioned within finely tuned microarchitectures defined by chemical gradients, boundaries, and mechanical cues – features that are essential for proper tissue function and homeostasis.

pmc-13055520.title: Alkali metal cation effects for rapid C–H activation by iron(0) complexes
pmc-13055520.creator: Nereida Hidalgo, Kendal W. Southwell, Ryan S. Donnelly, Brandon Q. Mercado, Sebastian M. Krajewski, Xiaoping Wang, Patrick L. Holland
pmc-13055520.description: Ion pairing with alkali metal cations offers a novel way to enhance the rate of C–H activation. This strategy is demonstrated here using diketiminate-supported iron(0) complexes, which previously were shown to activate the C–H bond of benzene slowly (hours at room temperature) and did not reach completion before decomposition.

pmc-13259540.title: Characterization of Motorcyclist Aggressive Driving Behavior in Urban and Suburban Environments: A Case Study of a Single Motorcyclist
pmc-13259540.creator: Libânia Mendes, Andreia Teixeira, Rute Carvalho, Isabel Barroso, Jaime Sampaio, Vítor Rodrigues
pmc-13259540.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Environment-specific acceleration and braking thresholds differed substantially between the urban and suburban motorcycle routes.Most riding behavior was classified as normal, while suburban riding showed fewer but higher-intensity acceleration and braking events. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13323393.title: Circulating IL-33 as a sensitive alarmin in systemic lupus erythematosus: a biomarker for disease activity and skin-specific manifestations
pmc-13323393.creator: Li Li, Xi Tan, Chen Zhao, Sijian Wen, Wenyu Li, Runge Fan, Wei Hou, Youkun Lin
pmc-13323393.description: Interleukin-33 (IL-33), an alarmin predominantly released by keratinocytes and endothelial cells, plays a pivotal role in type 2 immune responses and has been linked to the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study aimed to explore the relationship between plasma IL-33 levels and clinical features in SLE patients.

pmc-13476699.title: Cumulative Early‐Life Adversities Predict Short‐ and Long‐Term Survival in a Critically Endangered Lemur ( Propithecus verreauxi )
pmc-13476699.creator: Claudia Fichtel, Peter M. Kappeler
pmc-13476699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Adversities in early life compromise fitness components later in life, but the cumulative effects of multiple adversities and their timing across the lifespan remain poorly understood. To contribute comparative data from an independent primate radiation, we leverage long‐term demographic data from a wild lemur population to examine the effects of maternal loss, presence of an older sibling, maternal age, group size, temperature and rainfall on survival of 242 infants across the lifespan.

pmc-13544451.title: Alliance Ruptures and Psychotherapy Outcomes: A Multilevel Meta‐Analysis of Their Association
pmc-13544451.creator: A. Babl, J. M. Gómez Penedo, C. Nimphy, M. Keßel, C. Crainic, N. Boendermaker, C. F. Eubanks
pmc-13544451.description: ObjectiveAlthough two meta‐analyses have examined the relationship between rupture repair and treatment outcome, no meta‐analysis to date has investigated the association between alliance ruptures and treatment outcome. Numerous primary studies have explored this relationship; however, the methods used to assess ruptures vary considerably.
